# BabyLM eval set {#sec-eval}

{{< include _caution.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

DATA = Path("data")
ITEMS = pd.read_csv(DATA / "test_set.csv")
ALTS = [c for c in ITEMS.columns if c.startswith("alt_")]
TITLES = {
    "VL": "VL intransitive locative",
    "VOL": "VOL caused motion",
    "VO": "VO transitive",
    "VOO": "VOO ditransitive",
}
n = len(ITEMS)
n_per = ITEMS.groupby("construction_type").size()
n_verb = ITEMS.groupby("construction_type")["verb"].nunique()
n_corp = ITEMS["corpus"].nunique()
corpora = ", ".join(sorted(ITEMS["corpus"].astype(str).unique()))
```

`{python} n` adult CHILDES utterances from corpora in `tokens_filled.parquet` that are absent from childes-db 2021.1 (`{python} corpora`). Each construction uses up to 10 verbs whose highest adult schematic-VAC share is that frame, ranked by adult frame frequency. Items are round-robin stratified across those verbs. Five distractors per item have <10% adult share in the same frame and are inflected like the original verb.

Proper nouns, child speakers, fragments, fillers, and unintelligible `xxx` tokens are excluded. Frozen BabyLM `verb_sets.json` / ranking / affinity banks are unchanged.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-verbs
#| echo: false
pd.DataFrame({
    "VAC": list(TITLES),
    "Items": [int(n_per.get(c, 0)) for c in TITLES],
    "Verbs": [
        ", ".join(ITEMS.loc[ITEMS.construction_type.eq(c), "verb"].drop_duplicates())
        for c in TITLES
    ],
})
```

## Examples

Prefix / verb / suffix split the sentence at the CHILDES verb token so distractors can be spliced in.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-examples
#| echo: false
rows = []
for cons in TITLES:
    sub = ITEMS.loc[ITEMS.construction_type.eq(cons)].head(4)
    for _, r in sub.iterrows():
        rows.append({
            "VAC": cons,
            "Verb": r.verb,
            "Prep": "" if pd.isna(r.preposition) else r.preposition,
            "Sentence": r.sentence,
            "Alts": ", ".join(str(r[c]) for c in ALTS),
        })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```
